```{python}
# Question we are trying to answer.
# "Which breed groups are the most adopted?."
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
```

Download the [qr-sample.csv](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X9anHDY1FY_sJV9_AcRpU6YuCOZN5qqi/view?usp=sharing) file onto your computer and drag into this Notebook.

```{python}
# Create a dataframe from our csv file
# Question we are trying to answer
# "Which breed groups are the most adopted?."
df = pd.read_csv("/content/QR-Sample.csv")
```

df.columns

df.head()

#Group by Breed Group

```{python}
df.groupby('Breed group')[['Total Dogs Available']].sum()
```

# Bar Chart

```{python}
#Use this code if you want to create a bar chart
#Fill in the approriate columns and plot title and labels.
# Create a new dataframe, and group all of the Breed groups together
grouped_data = df.groupby(['Breed group']).sum()
#print the data
print(grouped_data)

# The next statement narrows down the dataframe to just the column you want
grouped_data = grouped_data['Number of dogs adopted']
grouped_data.plot.bar(tick_label=str)
# Print title and axis labels
plt.xlabel(" ")
plt.ylabel(" ")
plt.title("  ")
plt.show()
```

# Donut or Pie Chart

```{python}
#Use this code if you want to create a Donut or pie chart
#Fill in the approriate columns and plot title and labels.
# Create a new dataframe, and group all of the Breed Groups together
grouped_data = df.groupby(['Breed group']).sum()

# The next statement narrows down the dataframe to just the column you want
grouped_data = grouped_data['Number of dogs adopted']

grouped_data.plot.pie(figsize=(14, 7), autopct='%1.1f%%', subplots=True)

# The next 3 statements add a white circle to draw a donut chart
my_circle=plt.Circle( (0,0), 0.5, color='white')
p=plt.gcf()
p.gca().add_artist(my_circle)

# Print title and axis labels
plt.xlabel(" ")
plt.ylabel(" ")
plt.title(" ")
```

# Bar Chart with Percentages

```{python}

dogs_available = df.groupby("Breed group")["Total Dogs Available"].sum()
#print(dogs_available)

dogs_adopted = df.groupby(["Breed group"])["Number of dogs adopted"].sum().fillna(0)
#print(dogs_adopted)

dogs_percent = 100 * dogs_adopted / dogs_available
print(dogs_percent)

dogs_percent.plot.bar(tick_label=str)
```

#Scatter Plot

```{python}
# Create the scatter plot, specify two column names for x and y axis
# Both columns are quantitative (numbers).
df.plot.scatter(x="Total Dogs Available", y="Number of dogs adopted", figsize=(10,8))

# Plot lines at the weights that divide dogs into small (< 12 year), 
# medium (13 - 15 years), and large (> 15 years) categories.
# plt.axvline() plots a vertical line, plt.axhline() plots a horizontal line
plt.axvline(x=20, color="r", label="Small - Medium")
plt.axvline(x=30, color="g", label="Medum - Large")

# Add labels to the chart
plt.title("Total Dogs Available vs Number of dogs adopted")
plt.xlabel("Total Dogs Available")
plt.ylabel("Number of dogs adopted")
```
